content.text:
The Agent SDK does not solve subscription OAuth for a web app.

There are three distinct things:

- OpenAI Agents SDK uses the Responses API with Platform credentials and usage-based API billing. A ChatGPT subscription does not authenticate it.
- OpenAI Codex SDK can reuse a user’s ChatGPT subscription, but it runs a local Codex process. Twyne could support this in its desktop app by launching `codex login`; it cannot provide the same capability from the hosted web app. [OpenAI Codex authentication](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth), [Codex SDK](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk)
- Anthropic Agent SDK explicitly does not permit third-party products to offer Claude.ai login or consume users’ Free/Pro/Max limits without prior approval. Anthropic requires API-key or supported cloud-provider authentication for that use case. [Anthropic Agent SDK overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview), [authentication policy](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#authentication-and-credential-use)

So the viable product is:

- Twyne desktop: “Sign in with ChatGPT” through the local Codex SDK, consuming the user’s Codex subscription.
- Twyne web: Responses API through an OpenAI API key.
- Anthropic: API key by default; subscription sign-in only if Anthropic grants Twyne explicit partner approval.
- Keep provider credentials local and show the exact billing source in Settings.

Also, the `ant auth login` layer I added authenticates an Anthropic Console workspace—it does not turn a Claude Pro/Max subscription into Twyne inference. I should relabel or remove it rather than imply otherwise.
